title: Release 3.0.0 obligations
description: What the published contract owes at the major bump, and the followers a bump stales.
desiredOutcome: Every promise COMPATIBILITY.md dated to this release is delivered in code, and the document records it as delivered rather than pending.

tasks.title: The deprecation the contract dated to this release is delivered
tasks.description: DONE MEANS: a tests.add entry naming no file is a FINDING for a tdd task that is not done or cancelled, and the published contract records the deprecation as delivered rather than pending. COMPATIBILITY.md promises it in its own words - from 2.3.0 an entry naming no file is a warning whose text names the release the refusal arrives in, and at 3.0.0 it becomes a finding - and that document is a contract rather than a description, so shipping the major without it makes the document false. MEASURED BEFORE DECIDING: zero entries in this project's own plan and zero in the shipped example name no file, so the flip costs neither. The warning's text currently announces the future refusal; a finding announces nothing, it refuses, and the sentence has to change with it - including the pointer to the repair script, which is still the right advice for a plan written before the rule. The terminal and non-tdd exemptions stay exactly as they are: a settled task's tests.add is a record of work already judged.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__manifest_phases.py: a tests.add entry naming no file on a live tdd task is a finding, while the terminal and non-tdd exemptions stay silent

outcome.technical: The unnamed tests.add entry is appended to findings rather than warnings for a graded task, the announcing clause is removed from its text and from three documents that repeated it, and repair-tests-add.py excludes this rule's own finding from the two validator gates that would otherwise stop it repairing the entries it exists for.
outcome.descriptive: The deprecation the contract dated to this release refuses instead of warning, and the script that repairs it still runs.
